prose.summary: The product meets the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED. See the checklist below for the steps to claim.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 32091010, described as Acrylic emulsion (paint). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: The India-UAE CEPA applies. The normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) for each non-originating input and value addition (VA) of at least 40% on a FOB basis. The last manufacturing step took place in the UAE, and the work done goes beyond the simple operations that alone would not confer origin. Both non-originating inputs are classified outside subheading 320910, satisfying the CTSH requirement. The value addition is 65.0% on a FOB basis, exceeding the 40% threshold, so the product meets the rule of origin.

notes.text: For a retrospective certificate, the agreement specifies box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, while India's form uses box 9. India's form governs entry into India.
The CEPA requires document retention for 5 years, even though UAE law sets a minimum of 3 years.
The '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Indian inputs count as originating only with proof of their originating status (bilateral cumulation, Art. 3.7).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

Only for a certificate issued retrospectively: the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
Assumes the certificate's invoice value equals the shipment value given.
